question.problem:
The distance $d$ between the easternmost and westernmost points of the contiguous United States measures $2,693.1\,\text{mi}$ to the nearest tenth of a mile. Determine the upper and lower bounds of this measurement.

{{field-1}}$\text{mi}$
$\,\le d<$
{{field-2}}$\text{mi}$
question.worked_solution:
Our measurement is given to the nearest $0.1\,\text{mi}.$ So, the greatest possible error of this measurement is

$$
\frac{0.1\,\text{mi}}{2}=0.05\,\text{mi}.
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the lower and upper bounds of this measurement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{lower bound} & =2,693.1\,\text{mi}-0.05\,\text{mi} \\  & =2,693.05\,\text{mi} \\ \text{upper bound} & =2,693.1\,\text{mi}+0.05\,\text{mi} \\  & =2,693.15\,\text{mi}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the exact value of $d$ lies between the lower and upper bound, we conclude that

$$
2,693.05\,\text{mi}\le d<2,693.15\,\text{mi}.
$$
